transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

dE = door error. The machine doesn't think the door is closed or locked, even if it looks shut. Try these in order:

1. Power reset
• Unplug it (or flip the breaker) for about 5-10 minutes.
• While unplugged, press and hold Start/Pause for 5 seconds to drain leftover power.
• Plug back in, close the door firmly, and try again.

2. Check for anything blocking the door
• Look for clothing, a sock, or a towel caught in the rubber gasket or door edge.
• Make sure the load isn't so big it's pushing on the door.

3. Check the latch
• Door hook (the plastic/metal tongue on the door): Is it bent, loose, cracked, or broken?
• Latch hole on the machine: Clean out any lint, gunk, or detergent buildup.
• Close the door with a firm push until you hear a click.

4. Check for sagging
• If the door hinge is loose, the hook may not line up with the latch. Lift the door slightly while closing it and see if it catches.

5. Note the exact code (if it shows more than "dE")
• dE1: The door isn't detected as closed. Usually the hook, latch, or something blocking it.
• dE2: The door closed but won't lock. Usually a faulty door lock assembly.

If none of that works: The door lock/switch assembly has probably failed. It's a common, fairly cheap part (about $20-60) and an easy DIY swap on most models. Search your model number (on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back) plus "door lock." Less often, it's the wiring or control board, which is a job for a technician. If it's still under warranty, call LG.

Is it a front loader or a top loader? And does it show dE, dE1, or dE2? That would help narrow it down.
its a front loader, just says dE. its only when i put mum's king size duvet in tho, normal loads are fine

That's the giveaway. The duvet is too bulky, so it's pressing against the inside of the door or getting caught in the rubber seal, and the latch can't click shut properly. The machine itself is probably fine.

Things to try:
• Check the seal. Run your hand around the rubber gasket and make sure no fabric is tucked into it or poking out by the door.
• Load it differently. Don't stuff it in folded flat. Loosely roll or concertina it and feed it in so it sits toward the back of the drum, not against the door.
• Push it back before closing. If you have to lean on the door to shut it, it's too full.
• Use the Bedding/Bulky cycle if your machine has one.

Is your machine big enough? A king duvet generally needs a drum of about 9-10kg or more (check the capacity on the sticker or in the manual). If yours is smaller, it may not fit properly no matter how you load it. Forcing it is also hard on the machine: a soaked king duvet gets very heavy and can strain the drum, bearings, and door latch over time.

If it won't fit:
• Take it to a launderette. They have big drum machines for exactly this, and it's usually only a few pounds.
• Some dry cleaners will wash duvets too.

As long as normal loads still work, there's nothing wrong with your washer. It's just being asked to swallow more than it can handle.
